heading: ## 06 — #6 THE GREAT PYRAMID OF GIZA, EGYPT
text: Number six: the Great Pyramid, built for the pharaoh Khufu around four thousand five hundred years ago. It originally stood about a hundred and forty-six point six metres tall, from an estimated two point three million blocks, its sides aligned to the cardinal directions with remarkable, though not perfect, accuracy. Here, the evidence is strong. Most core limestone was quarried on the plateau itself. Finer casing stone came from Tura, across the Nile. Papyri found at Wadi al-Jarf include the logbook of an official named Merer, recording his crew shipping that limestone to Giza by boat. Egyptian art shows loads dragged on sledges, and a workers' town has been excavated nearby. What we don't know is the ramp system. Straight, zigzag, spiralling: each has supporters. None is proven. But so far, every builder had farming behind them. The next site breaks that rule.
previous_text: On Rapa Nui, the challenge was about a thousand statues. In Egypt, it was over two million blocks.
next_text: Number five: Göbekli Tepe, in south-eastern Türkiye. Its monumental enclosures date to roughly ninety-six hundred to eighty-two hundred B.C.E., around seven thousand years before the Great Pyramid.
